cands.name: Liz Ortega
cands.bio: Liz Ortega (Ortega-Toro) is a Democratic member of the California State Assembly for District 20, in office since December 2022. She was previously statewide political director for AFSCME Local 3299 and the first Latina executive secretary-treasurer of the Alameda Labor Council. She lives in San Leandro.

cands.gaps: We found no record of her sponsored bills or specific actions in office on data centers, property taxes, foreign or investor purchases of land and homes, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, guns, or school choice. We found no statement from her on data centers or on new development. Her 2022 survey describes neighborhood policing and funding for anti-gang and drug prevention programs, but not specific police pay or penalty positions. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys, so her stated positions come mostly from 2022. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 90: Wikipedia says she was born in Guadalajara, Mexico, came to the U.S. at age three, and was raised and attended public school in Oakland; she now lives in San Leandro.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since December 2022, chairing the Labor and Employment Committee. Before that she was statewide political director for AFSCME Local 3299 (2013-2017), lobbying the Legislature, and headed the Alameda Labor Council as executive secretary-treasurer from 2017. She was also its political director from 2011 to 2013.
qual.why: Nearly four years of legislative service plus a career as a legislative and political director who lobbied the Legislature fits the high band for writing law and budgets. Committee seats and the chair role were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: In her 2022 Ballotpedia survey she described herself as a strong advocate for women's reproductive freedoms and healthcare, and urged a Yes vote on Proposition 1 to preserve abortion rights.

cands.name: Patricia Muga
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 20 in 2026. UCLA graduate with a past career in telecommunications, including network, sales and administrative management work. Now a licensed real estate appraiser and broker. Election worker and Vote Center Captain for 12 years. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists these endorsements and voter guide recommendations for her Assembly run: Reform California; The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn; April's Common Sense Cali Voters; Based in Malibu; Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide.

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace, where she grew up, or when she came to California. No stated positions were found on data centers, homestead property taxes, investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion, or teacher pay. She has not held elected office, so there are no deeds to report. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. No news coverage or controversies about her were found. Her campaign site's 'Endorsed by' section showed no readable names.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Career in telecommunications (technical network, sales and administrative management), now a licensed California Certified General Real Estate Appraiser and Real Estate Broker. Earlier worked as an EMT and as a government relations assistant for a Los Angeles County medical center. Has been an election worker for 12 years and has testified before the Legislature. No elected office is documented.
qual.why: Management and licensed-professional work in business and real estate puts her in the middle band. No prior legislative service or policy or budget career is documented, so she scores no higher.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports full funding for local law enforcement, opposes legislation that reduces penalties for violent or repeat offenders, and wants to restore prosecutorial tools.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports parental rights, school choice and holding schools accountable for student outcomes. It gives no teacher pay position.
